title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 1986 'Analysis situs (première mouture)', Grothendieck builds an axiomatic, combinatorial model of a 'tame' space, which he calls a contrée. The data are:
- a set M of 'multiplicités' (cell- or piece-like objects);
- a relation ≪, apparently meaning 'lies in';
- a relation 𝔞, apparently compatibility or admissibility;
- a family F of 'figures'. A figure is a finite set of multiplicities ordered by a face relation ≤, satisfying axioms Fig 1–Fig 4. The contrée satisfies axioms Cont 1–Cont 5.
- a set L ⊂ M of point-like elements ('lieux'). Each X has a shadow (ombre) X̃ = L_X ⊂ L, presumably the points ≪ X.

On p.36 (Scholie a–c), for a fixed figure F:
- X ↦ X̃ is injective, and its image F̃ is a 'divisible' family of subsets of L.
- The 'open cells' X̃° = X̃ ∖ ∂X̃ are nonempty and partition the shadow L_F of F.
- The face order ≤ on F is inclusion of shadows.

This is the familiar picture of a regular cell complex, recovered from its point set together with its closed cells.

Page 37, item d). For every sub-figure F' of F, its image F̃' has union the shadow L_{F'} ⊂ L. The map F' ↦ F̃' is a bijection between:
- the sub-figures of F, and
- the subsets of F̃ (or of the shadow of F) that are 'closed' for the closure structure that the closed cells X̃ (X ∈ F) define.

In modern terms: sub-figures (subcomplexes) correspond exactly to the closed unions of closed cells. This is the subcomplex ↔ downward-closed-set-of-faces ↔ closed-union-of-cells dictionary.

Proposition (stability under restriction). Let M be a contrée and M' ⊂ M a sub-contrée, i.e. a subset closed downward under ≪. Equip M' with:
- the induced relations ≪_{M'} and 𝔞_{M'};
- F_{M'} = the figures of M contained in M'.

Then:
- (M', ≪_{M'}, F_{M'}) satisfies Cont 1–Cont 4.
- For X ∈ M', its combinatorial and geometric dimensions are the same in M and in M'.
- With L' = M' ∩ L, the shadow of a figure F ∈ F_{M'} is the same computed in M or in M'. The same holds for the shadow of X and for its boundary ∂X.
- Fig 1–Fig 4 hold in M'.
- The page breaks off; p.38 adds that Cont 5 is also stable under passage to a sub-contrée.

Purpose. These are the standard heredity results needed before working locally in this axiomatic tame topology. For example, they let one restrict to the closure of one multiplicity, the analogue of passing to a closed definable subset or a subcomplex. Pages 38ff go on to define disjoint figures and the refinement order 'F plus fine que G'.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The proposition is stated without proof, and its truth depends on the exact form of Cont 1–Cont 5, which are on earlier pages. Hereditary closure under ≪ is what makes it plausible: elementary figures F_X and refinements consist of elements ≪ elements already in M', so they stay inside M'.

In d), the closure notion is only gestured at ('fermées' in quotes, with an unclear phrase about 'la rel. d'admissibilité'). It must be read as: unions of closed cells X̃ that contain, along with each cell, all of its faces. Without that precise meaning the bijection claim is ambiguous.

ideas.what: Bijection between sub-figures of a figure and the 'closed' unions of closed cells in its shadow
ideas.modern_name: Subcomplexes of a regular CW/cell complex ↔ down-closed subsets of the face poset ↔ closed unions of cells (Alexandrov topology on the face poset)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (J.H.C. Whitehead's CW complexes; Alexandrov's finite-space topology; face-poset combinatorics, e.g. Björner)

ideas.what: Sub-contrée (subset closed under ≪) inherits the axioms Cont 1–5 and Fig 1–4, with dimensions, shadows and boundaries unchanged
ideas.modern_name: Heredity of a tame/o-minimal-type structure to closed definable subsets; restriction of a stratified space or cell complex to a closed union of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in o-minimality (van den Dries) and stratification theory

ideas.what: Overall axiomatic notion of 'contrée' (multiplicités, figures, shadows in a set of lieux), an abstract combinatorial model of tame topology
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic tame topology; closest to o-minimal structures / face posets of regular cell decompositions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Programme announced by Grothendieck in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (1984); o-minimality developed by van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme announces 'topologie modérée' only programmatically; the 'contrée' axiomatics itself seems unpublished

missed.claim: This page is a routine heredity lemma inside Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatisation of tame topology ('contrées'). The axiom system as a whole is an unpublished attempt at what Esquisse §5 called 'topologie modérée', but this particular page adds nothing beyond standard subcomplex/restriction facts.
missed.quote: Soit M une contrée, M' une sous contrée, i.e. une partie de M, fermée par ≪ ... satisfait les conditions Cont 1 à Cont 4
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is only of documentary interest, for comparing Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics with o-minimality and with poset models of stratified spaces (exit-path / Alexandrov-space approaches).

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard verifications: subcomplexes correspond to closed unions of cells, and the axioms restrict to sub-contrées. The only interest is that they sit inside an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology framework, and nothing on this page itself is new.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'on a 𝓛_F F̃' = L_F ⊂ L au voisinage' more likely reads 'on a F̃' = L_{F'} ⊂ L son ombre' (the struck-out letter is a false start; 'au voisinage' looks like 'son ombre').
'de F̃ (ouvertes[?] de F)' more likely reads 'de F̃ (ombre de F)'.

'son ouverture (fermeture)[?] pour M ou M' est la =' should be 'son ombre pour M ou M' est la même'. The interlined word above appears to be a parenthetical such as '(généralisée)'; it is uncertain, but not 'fermeture'.
'si si X ∈ M', ses ouvertes[?] est la =' should be 'et si X ∈ M', son ombre est la même pour M et pour M'', followed by 'de même pour le bord ∂X'.
'rel. d'admissibilité de F̃ par les X̃' is uncertain; it may be '(top.) définie sur F̃ par les X̃'.
